topic: Is-A vs. Has-A Relationships in Inheritance
explanation: A fundamental design principle in C++ class design involves understanding the difference between "Is-A" and "Has-A" relationships.  Choosing the correct relationship significantly impacts code maintainability, extensibility, and correctness.  'Is-A' implies inheritance (public inheritance specifically), where a derived class is a specialized version of a base class. 'Has-A' implies composition, where a class contains another class as a member. Misusing inheritance when a 'Has-A' relationship is appropriate leads to tight coupling, inflexible designs, and potential violations of the Liskov Substitution Principle.
keywords: Is-A vs Has-A, inheritance vs composition, C++ class relationships
